newsitem.title: USA: ConAgra sees double-digit EPS rise for FY97.
newsitem.headline: ConAgra sees double-digit EPS rise for FY97.

text.p: ConAgra Inc said Thursday it continues to expect double-digit earnings per share growth and record earnings for 1997.
Earlier, it reported earnings for the second quarter ended November 24 of $0.82 a share, up from $0.72 a year ago.
"Our second quarter results extend ConAgra's record as the food industry leader in consistent, strong long-term earnings growth," Philip Fletcher, chairman, said in a statement.

ConAgra said its grocery/diversified products' operating profit was up 30 percent in the second quarter and 26 percent in the first half, compared with a year ago. Sales in this segment increased 12 percent in the second quarter and 10 percent in the first half.

Unit volume grew nine percent in the second quarter and eight percent in the first half, enabling the Hunt-Wesson and ConAgra Frozen Foods businesses both to increase operating profit well over 20 percent in both periods.
ConAgra's refrigerated foods operating profit fell 28 percent in the quarter and 20 percent in the first half.
ConAgra said it expects significant refrigerated foods operating profit growth in the second half of fiscal 1997.

Segment sales decreased three percent in the second quarter and four percent in the first half of fiscal 1997 primarily due to beef and poultry operations divested or restructured during and after last year's second quarter.
Branded processed meats operating profit rose strongly in the second quarter and was up in the first half, it said.
U.S. beef earnings declined sharply in both periods, while Australia beef results improved in both periods.
Second quarter and first half operating profit decreased in the pork business. But ConAgra said pork earnings were "more than satisfactory" given high raw material costs.

Pressured by high feed ingredients costs, poultry products operating profit was down in both periods. Cheese business profits were down moderately in the second quarter and up moderately in the first half.

In food inputs and ingredients, operating profit grew 15 percent in the second quarter and 19 percent in the first half of fiscal 1997, compared with a year ago. Segment sales rose four percent in the second quarter and three percent in the first half. Excluding business dispositions and acquisitions, first half segment sales increased nearly 5 percent.
